answer: Sybil resistance works when each new identity must bond scarce, non-transferable stake that decays unless peers repeatedly attest real work. Treat that bond like an ivory seal: costly to mint, worthless to clone. A fresh agent may only whisper its first claims into a slow queue; peers grade those claims and attach a plume of attestations that unlocks spendable weight. Without enough peer plumes, the clone cannot tip markets or vote, so flooding identities burns capital faster than it earns influence.
